slug: soot
title: Soot-style IR and whole-program analysis infrastructure
module: soot_analysis.py
description: >
  Build the Jimple-like intermediate representation and the core
  whole-program analysis utilities on top of the shared program model:
  the scene registry, CHA call-graph construction, copy propagation,
  and dead-code elimination. This layer is the foundation that the
  FlowDroid and StubDroid layers build upon.
contract:
  - id: jimple-ir
    text: >
      Provide a Jimple-like IR view (JimpleBody) over MethodBody with
      indexed units, locals, this/parameter locals, statement lookup by
      id, and CFG successor computation covering linear fall-through,
      conditional branches (if with true/false targets) and returns.
  - id: scene-registry
    text: >
      Provide a Scene registry that loads a Program and indexes classes,
      methods (by full Soot-style signature), the type hierarchy
      (super classes and interfaces), entry points, and supports
      upward method lookup through super classes.
  - id: cha-call-graph
    text: >
      Provide CHACallGraphBuilder that computes a class-hierarchy-
      analysis call graph starting from the program entry points:
      every call site is resolved to the method found in the receiver's
      declared class (or its super classes) plus overriding methods in
      all known subclasses; the graph exposes edges, per-method
      callers/callees and the set of reachable methods.
  - id: copy-propagation
    text: >
      Provide copy propagation over Jimple bodies: for copy statements
      `x = y` replace subsequent uses of x by y until x or y is
      redefined, covering rhs, rhs_vars, call args, receivers, field
      bases and branch conditions; report the number of replaced uses.
  - id: dead-code-elimination
    text: >
      Provide dead-code elimination over Jimple bodies using
      CFG-based liveness: remove side-effect-free statements (assign,
      new, nop) whose defined local is not live, never removing
      sources, sinks, calls, returns, branches, field stores or
      identity statements; report the number of removed statements.
  - id: standalone
    text: >
      The module runs standalone via `python3 soot_analysis.py
      [benchmark_dir]`, analyzing every benchmark and emitting
      `KEY: VALUE` lines including LAYER, BENCHMARK, CLASSES, METHODS,
      STATEMENTS, ENTRY_POINTS, CALL_GRAPH_EDGES, REACHABLE_METHODS,
      COPY_PROPAGATIONS, DEAD_STATEMENTS_REMOVED and TOTAL_* aggregates.

slug: flowdroid
title: FlowDroid-style IFDS taint analysis
module: flowdroid_analysis.py
depends_on: [soot]
description: >
  Add a FlowDroid-style IFDS taint analysis on top of the Jimple-like
  IR and the CHA call graph from the Soot layer, including access
  paths, taint facts, alias support, source/sink handling and
  lifecycle-aware propagation. Calls that cannot be resolved to an
  application method body fall back to a conservative default taint
  wrapper (tainted arguments or receiver taint the return value and
  the receiver object).
contract:
  - id: access-paths
    text: >
      Provide AccessPath (base local plus field sequence), SourceInfo
      and TaintFact types; facts carry their originating source so
      leaks can be attributed to a source method and category.
  - id: source-sink-handling
    text: >
      Provide SourceSinkManager resolving sources/sinks both from
      statement flags (is_source/is_sink with categories) and from the
      program's source_sink_spec; source calls generate taint on their
      left-hand side, sink calls with a tainted argument record a leak.
  - id: ifds-solver
    text: >
      Provide IFDSTaintAnalysis performing flow-sensitive forward
      propagation over the interprocedural supergraph with per-method
      worklists, call-to-callee seed mapping (arguments to parameters,
      receiver to this), return-value and receiver write-back, and
      memoized per-context method summaries with a recursion guard.
  - id: field-sensitivity
    text: >
      Field stores taint base.field (weak update), field loads taint
      the target when the base's matching field or the whole base
      object is tainted.
  - id: alias-support
    text: >
      Copy assignments create alias groups (union-find per body);
      tainting a field through one alias is visible when loading the
      same field through any other alias.
  - id: lifecycle-aware
    text: >
      Taint stored into Android component fields in one entry point is
      visible on `this` in every other entry point of the same
      component via shared component field state and a whole-program
      fixpoint over the lifecycle entry points.
  - id: standalone
    text: >
      The module runs standalone via `python3 flowdroid_analysis.py
      [benchmark_dir]`, emitting `KEY: VALUE` lines including LAYER,
      BENCHMARK, EXPECTED_LEAKS, DETECTED_LEAKS, TRUE_POSITIVES,
      FALSE_POSITIVES, MISSED_LEAKS, LEAK, TAINT_FACTS_GENERATED,
      METHODS_ANALYZED and aggregate TOTAL_* plus PRECISION, RECALL, F1.
verification:
  - All seven benchmarks under benchmarks/ are analyzed; every expected
    leak in expected_leaks is detected (matched by source_method and
    sink_method) and no false positives are reported, including the
    no-leak benchmark.

"""
End-to-end and unit tests for the static-analysis stack.

Runs with plain `python3 agent_tests/test_stack.py` (exit code 0 on
success) or under pytest.
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from program_model import load_all_benchmarks, load_program  # noqa: E402
from soot_analysis import (  # noqa: E402
    CHACallGraphBuilder,
    CopyPropagator,
    DeadCodeEliminator,
    JimpleBody,
    Scene,
    analyze_program,
)
from flowdroid_analysis import IFDSTaintAnalysis, match_leaks  # noqa: E402
from stubdroid_analysis import (  # noqa: E402
    StubDroidAnalysis,
    SummaryGenerator,
)

BENCH = os.path.join(ROOT, "benchmarks")
PROGRAMS = {p.name: p for p in load_all_benchmarks(BENCH)}

EXPECTED_LEAK_COUNTS = {
    "SimpleFlow": 1,
    "FieldSensitivity": 1,
    "InterProcedural": 1,
    "AliasHandling": 1,
    "LifecycleCallbacks": 1,
    "LibrarySummary": 1,
    "NoLeak": 0,
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Soot layer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_scene_registry():
    scene = Scene().load_program(PROGRAMS["InterProcedural"])
    assert len(scene.classes) == 3
    assert scene.get_method("<com.example.InterActivity: void onCreate(android.os.Bundle)>")
    entries = {m.signature.method_name for m in scene.entry_points}
    assert entries == {"onCreate"}
    # upward lookup: not found in scene superclasses -> None
    assert scene.lookup_method("com.example.InterActivity", "obfuscate", 1) is not None


def test_cha_call_graph():
    program = PROGRAMS["InterProcedural"]
    scene = Scene().load_program(program)
    graph = CHACallGraphBuilder(scene).build()
    callees = graph.callees_of(
        "<com.example.InterActivity: void onCreate(android.os.Bundle)>"
    )
    assert "<com.example.InterActivity: java.lang.String obfuscate(java.lang.String)>" in callees
    assert "<com.example.InterActivity: void sendData(java.lang.String)>" in callees
    assert "<android.telephony.TelephonyManager: java.lang.String getDeviceId()>" in callees
    into = graph.callers_of(
        "<android.telephony.SmsManager: void sendTextMessage(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String,android.app.PendingIntent,android.app.PendingIntent)>"
    )
    assert "<com.example.InterActivity: void sendData(java.lang.String)>" in into


def test_jimple_body_cfg():
    method = PROGRAMS["SimpleFlow"].classes[-1].methods[0]
    body = JimpleBody(method)
    assert len(body) == 6
    assert body.stmt_index(3) == 3
    assert body.successors(5) == []  # return
    assert body.successors(0) == [1]


def test_copy_propagation_and_dce():
    stats = analyze_program(PROGRAMS["AliasHandling"])
    # r5 = r4 copy: the field load through r5 is rewritten to r4 and the
    # then-dead copy is removed.
    assert stats["copy_propagations"] >= 1
    assert stats["dead_statements_removed"] >= 1


def test_dce_never_removes_sinks_or_calls():
    for program in PROGRAMS.values():
        scene = Scene().load_program(program)
        elim = DeadCodeEliminator()
        for method in scene.methods_with_bodies():
            body = JimpleBody(method)
            before = [s for s in body.units if s.kind in ("call", "return", "identity", "field_store")]
            elim.run(body)
            after = [s for s in body.units if s.kind in ("call", "return", "identity", "field_store")]
            assert {s.stmt_id for s in before} == {s.stmt_id for s in after}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FlowDroid layer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _check_leaks(analysis_cls, *extra):
    for name, program in PROGRAMS.items():
        analysis = analysis_cls(program, *extra).run() if extra else analysis_cls(program).run()
        tp, fp, missed = match_leaks(program, analysis.leaks)
        expected = EXPECTED_LEAK_COUNTS[name]
        assert missed == 0, f"{name}: missed {missed} of {expected} expected leaks"
        assert fp == 0, f"{name}: {fp} false positives"
        assert tp == expected, f"{name}: tp={tp} expected={expected}"


def test_flowdroid_leaks_all_benchmarks():
    _check_leaks(IFDSTaintAnalysis)


def test_flowdroid_alias_and_field_sensitivity():
    analysis = IFDSTaintAnalysis(PROGRAMS["AliasHandling"]).run()
    assert any(l.tainted_var == "r6" for l in analysis.leaks)
    analysis = IFDSTaintAnalysis(PROGRAMS["FieldSensitivity"]).run()
    assert any(l.tainted_var == "r5" for l in analysis.leaks)


def test_flowdroid_lifecycle():
    analysis = IFDSTaintAnalysis(PROGRAMS["LifecycleCallbacks"]).run()
    leak = analysis.leaks[0]
    assert leak.sink_method == "sendTextMessage"
    assert ("com.example.LifecycleActivity", "imei") in analysis.global_field_taint


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# StubDroid layer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_summary_generation():
    program = PROGRAMS["LibrarySummary"]
    scene = Scene().load_program(program)
    summaries = SummaryGenerator(scene).generate_for_program()
    add = summaries["<java.util.ArrayList: boolean add(java.lang.Object)>"]
    get = summaries["<java.util.ArrayList: java.lang.Object get(int)>"]
    put = summaries["<java.util.HashMap: java.lang.Object put(java.lang.Object,java.lang.Object)>"]
    assert "@parameter0 -> this._elements" in str(add)
    assert "this._elements -> @return" in str(get)
    assert "@parameter1 -> this._values" in str(put)


def test_stubdroid_leaks_all_benchmarks():
    for name, program in PROGRAMS.items():
        scene = Scene().load_program(program)
        summaries = SummaryGenerator(scene).generate_for_program()
        analysis = StubDroidAnalysis(program, summaries).run()
        tp, fp, missed = match_leaks(program, analysis.leaks)
        assert missed == 0 and fp == 0, f"{name}: missed={missed} fp={fp}"
        assert tp == EXPECTED_LEAK_COUNTS[name]


def test_stubdroid_summary_application():
    program = PROGRAMS["LibrarySummary"]
    scene = Scene().load_program(program)
    summaries = SummaryGenerator(scene).generate_for_program()
    analysis = StubDroidAnalysis(program, summaries).run()
    assert analysis.summary_applications >= 2  # ArrayList.add + ArrayList.get


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone modules and run.sh
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _run(cmd):
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONHASHSEED="0")
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return proc


def test_modules_run_standalone():
    for module in ("soot_analysis.py", "flowdroid_analysis.py", "stubdroid_analysis.py"):
        proc = _run([sys.executable, module])
        assert proc.returncode == 0, f"{module}: {proc.stderr}"
        assert "LAYER: " in proc.stdout


def test_run_sh_emits_key_value_lines():
    proc = _run(["bash", "run.sh"])
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    out = proc.stdout
    for key in (
        "EXPERIMENT:", "LAYER: soot", "LAYER: flowdroid", "LAYER: stubdroid",
        "CALL_GRAPH_EDGES:", "COPY_PROPAGATIONS:", "DEAD_STATEMENTS_REMOVED:",
        "EXPECTED_LEAKS:", "DETECTED_LEAKS:", "SUMMARIES_GENERATED:",
        "SUMMARY_APPLICATIONS:", "PRECISION:", "RECALL:", "F1:",
        "ALL_EXPECTED_LEAKS_FOUND: true", "RUN_STATUS: OK",
    ):
        assert key in out, f"missing {key!r} in run.sh output"


def main():
    tests = [(k, v) for k, v in sorted(globals().items()) if k.startswith("test_")]
    failed = 0
    for name, fn in tests:
        try:
            fn()
            print(f"PASS: {name}")
        except AssertionError as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL: {name}: {exc}")
    print(f"TESTS_PASSED: {len(tests) - failed}")
    print(f"TESTS_FAILED: {failed}")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
